title: Obstacle Course Challenge - ForgeBot-DD1
goal_description: Propose a supervised research mission for collision avoidance

hypotheses.title: Increasing Repulsion Gain
hypotheses.statement: Increasing the repulsion gain will make the robot more responsive to nearby obstacles, reducing the likelihood of collisions.
hypotheses.mechanism: The repulsion gain controls how strongly the robot reacts to obstacles in its path, which can be adjusted to increase or decrease the avoidance response.
contradicting_evidence: Experiment plan_1a9739fe: Observed delta=+0.000. Verdict: inconclusive (No statistically significant difference in collision count or success rate.). (Did not produce statistically distinguishable change)

hypotheses.title: Reducing Safety Margin
hypotheses.statement: Reducing the safety margin will allow the robot to come closer to obstacles, potentially increasing its efficiency but at the risk of increased collisions.
hypotheses.mechanism: The safety margin defines the buffer distance the robot maintains from obstacles. Lowering this value can make the robot more efficient but may increase the risk of collisions.
